# HamariHawa (ہماری ہوا · हमारी हवा, "our air")

> A free, non-commercial public-awareness site that shows, live, what satellites see in the air over Pakistan and North India (the Indus-Gangetic Plain, 25–35.5°N, 66–88.5°E): fires, smoke, nitrogen dioxide from traffic and industry, known pollution sources, and what the air means for health in 17 cities. In English, Urdu and Hindi.

## Pages
- [Live map](https://hamarihawa.org/): fire detections from the last 24 h / 48 h / 7 days, each named after the nearest village and tagged when it sits on a known brick kiln, landfill, industrial estate or always-hot site; satellite layers (14-day traffic & industry NO₂, haze/AOD, smoke index, true colour); live AQI and health estimates for Lahore, Karachi, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Gujranwala, Multan, Peshawar, Delhi, Gurugram, Amritsar, Ludhiana, Chandigarh, Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi and Patna; source shares from published studies; what can be done about transport.
- [Pollution sites](https://hamarihawa.org/sites/): traffic NO₂ hotspots, landfills with methane plumes, power and industrial plants with CO₂ plumes, always-hot industrial sites and the districts with the most brick kilns.
- [About, method and disclaimer](https://hamarihawa.org/about/): methods, limits, privacy, credits.
- [Use the data](https://hamarihawa.org/data/): Google Earth KML feed, how to use it in GIS tools, why Google Maps can't show live layers, JSON feeds and licences.
- [What's new](https://hamarihawa.org/updates/): dated list of additions and fixes, newest first. Atom feed: https://hamarihawa.org/updates/feed.xml
- [24-month Lahore and Islamabad air report](https://hamarihawa.org/report/).

## Google Earth, Google Maps and GIS
- One link opens the whole live map in Google Earth: https://hamarihawa.org/hamarihawa.kml (a KML of network links). Layers: fires in the last 24 h (refreshed every 15 min) and 7 days; US AQI and PM2.5 now in 17 cities (Copernicus CAMS model, every 30 min); 2-week Sentinel-5P traffic and industry NO₂ with labelled hotspots (daily); NASA GIBS haze/aerosol and VIIRS true-colour photo (daily, one day behind); pollution sites (landfills, plants with CO₂ plumes, fossil power plants, always-hot industrial sites, brick-kiln belts).
- Google Earth Pro: Add → Network Link with that URL; layers refresh on their own. Google Earth web/mobile: download and import the file; it loads the latest data when opened.
- Google Maps does not accept live third-party layers. Google My Maps imports KML as a static copy with a 2,000-place limit per layer, so it suits the pollution-sites layer (https://hamarihawa.org/kml/sources.kml) but not the live fires.
- Individual KML layers for QGIS, ArcGIS, Civil 3D or any KML reader: https://hamarihawa.org/fires.kml?hours=24 (also 48, 168), https://hamarihawa.org/kml/air.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/traffic.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/satellite.kml, https://hamarihawa.org/kml/sources.kml

## Open data (JSON). Fire feed and NO₂: CC BY 4.0. Pollution sites and kiln layers: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, because they include SentinelKilnDB). Landfills, industrial areas, power plants and roads: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/fires?hours=24 (also 48, 168): fire feed with stats, events and points. trend.prev is the count in the window just before; trend.days the last 14 daily totals.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/days: daily fire totals since 14 Oct 2026 (days on Pakistan time, UTC+5; distinct spots; pk, in, night, crop, frp). https://hamarihawa.org/api/day?d=YYYY-MM-DD gives that day's spots.
- https://hamarihawa.org/api/no2.json: 14-day NO₂ average metadata and labelled hotspots. Image: /api/no2.png (Web Mercator) or /api/no2-geo.png (equirectangular).
- https://hamarihawa.org/sources/sites.json: persistent pollution sites by category.
- https://hamarihawa.org/sources/kilns.json, osm-landfill.json, osm-industrial.json, plants.json, hotspots.json, carbonmapper.json, roads.json (major roads, context under the NO₂ layer): source layers.

## Key facts and methods
- Fires: NASA FIRMS near-real-time VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) and MODIS 1 km (Aqua, Terra). Satellites pass about 01:30 and 13:30 local time; data arrive about 3 hours later. Cloud cover at the last pass is drawn on the map, because fires under cloud can't be seen.
- Fire type: tagged as brick kiln, landfill, industrial or always-hot site when within reach of a known source; otherwise "likely crop burning" in Oct–Nov and Apr–May, "near a town" near big towns, or "open land". These are best guesses, not findings.
- Traffic NO₂: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI tropospheric NO₂ from NASA GIBS, 14-day average; ratios are against the median over the plains. In big-city cores NO₂ is mostly from vehicle engines. Pixels are about 5 km wide, so the layer shows a city's traffic as one hotspot and corridors such as the GT Road belt, not individual roads; major roads from OpenStreetMap are drawn underneath for context.
- Wind: 10 m wind from the Open-Meteo forecast API on a 1° grid (https://hamarihawa.org/api/wind; dir is where the wind comes from, km/h), refreshed every 30 minutes, drawn as drifting streaks; the Your-air box names the big towns the wind is coming from and heading towards.
- City air: Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo (about 11 km). In winter it reads lower than ground sensors in Lahore and Islamabad by roughly 1.5×.
- Health estimates: cigarettes ≈ PM2.5 ÷ 22 (Berkeley Earth); WHO 24-h guideline 15 µg/m³; life expectancy −0.098 years per µg/m³ above 5 if sustained (AQLI); extra daily deaths +0.68% per 10 µg/m³ above 15 (Liu et al., NEJM 2019). Population-level estimates only.
- Source shares (PM2.5): Lahore, PAQI 2025 (emitted): vehicles 35%, industry 28%, brick kilns 17%, waste 6%. Islamabad–Rawalpindi, PAQI 2025: vehicles 53%, kilns 18%, waste 11%, industry 9%. Punjab (Pakistan), World Bank 2024 (in the air): dust 25%, residential 23%, transport 16%, industry 16%, agriculture 13%, waste 7%. Delhi winter, TERI-ARAI 2018 (in the air): vehicles 28%, dust 17%, industry 16%, biomass 14%, residential 10%, brick kilns 8%, power 6%.

## Please cite as
HamariHawa (hamarihawa.org), using NASA FIRMS, NASA GIBS / Copernicus Sentinel-5P, Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo, Carbon Mapper, SentinelKilnDB, the Pakistan IGP Brick Kiln Dataset, OpenStreetMap and GeoNames.

## Caveats
Being shown on this site means satellites detected heat or pollution at a place; it does not identify who lit a fire or show that anyone broke the law.
